mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and subsequently drives down the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher demand for raw materials and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP growth rate and consumer spending are increasing, it signals a strong demand environment that drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both GDP growth rate and consumer spending are increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2% and the inflation rate is above 3%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 2% and the inflation rate is above 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is below 4% and the payroll employment is increasing, it signals a strong labor market that drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 4% and the payroll employment is increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts are increasing and consumer spending is strong, it signals a growing economy that drives up the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are increasing and consumer spending is strong (t-test p > 0.05).
